intro: Same prompt, four AIs, and us. Entertainment only. Graded at the Westgate SuperContest line each side was asked.
prompt_note: Asked Saturday Oct 31, 2026 on the Westgate SuperContest Week 8 lines. CAR @ GB (Thursday) is excluded. Top 5s are graded at flat 1 unit. All 13 games are pending.
score_source: ESPN NFL scoreboard week 8 seasontype 2 dates 2026, snapshot data/verified-finals-2026-11-07.json. All 13 games on this board are final. CAR @ GB is not on this board. Lines unchanged from the original Westgate board.

MIN@DET.reason: Detroit opened -4.5 and the money has pushed it toward Minnesota, and Caesars says it will likely need the Vikings and the under. No Vikings game since Week 1 has topped 39 combined points, Detroit is without S Kerby Joseph, and the hook over 3 matters in a 46-point game.

LV@NYJ.reason: Coin flip, but Vegas ranks 31st in EPA per rush and 32nd in rushing success, has allowed multiple passing TDs in five straight games and faces a 10 a.m. body-clock kickoff. The Jets' offense moves the ball and gets the softest defense it has seen.

ARI@DAL.reason: Arizona has given up 30 or more in six games, is again missing RG Jon Gaines and DT Walter Nolen, and stays with Brissett at Dallas. Dallas ran for 204 on Philly, sharps took the Cowboys at -6 and -6.5, and this 6.5 beats the books' 7.

ATL@TB.reason: Tampa's defense has quietly played at an elite level and Mayfield is back after an 11-attempt tune-up. Egbuka is out, so this rides the run game and the defense; the market cut Bijan's rushing line, a sign it expects Tampa's front to hold.

BAL@BUF.reason: Lamar returns against a Bills defense that ranks last in EPA per play and has allowed 30 or more four times. Sharp money moved books from Ravens +4 to +3, the SuperContest still gives the hook, and Kincaid, DJ Moore and Spencer Brown are all questionable for Buffalo.

IND@JAX.reason: The number jumped two full points on the Nelson and Buckner trades; power-rating models make it closer to 6.5. Jacksonville's run defense will bottle Taylor, but Lawrence's passing line has dropped 12 yards and this Jags offense is not built to run away. Warren is back for Jones.

TEN@CIN.reason: Tennessee traded Simmons on Thursday after giving up 491 yards to Cleveland and now plays without Tate and Spears. Cincinnati scored on five straight drives after a 13-0 halftime deficit in Baltimore; this 10.5 sits one to two points under the books, where sharps hit the Bengals from -7 up to -12.5.

CLE@PIT.reason: Watt, Highsmith and Ramsey are all in for a defense that held its last three opponents to 22, 19 and 10. Cleveland's wins keep coming by three to five points and it converts 32.6% on third down; the Paris hangover and the hook are the risks.

LAC@LAR.reason: The Chargers are 0-6 and 0-5-1 ATS and lose Derwin James and G Kayode Awosika. The Rams' run game got going against Vegas, and power-rating models show this as the biggest gap on the board.

KC@DEN.reason: Kansas City managed 213 yards in Seattle and still lacks a deep threat even with Rice back. Denver is 3-0 ATS at home and covered its one home-dog spot, sharps took Broncos +2, and Denver has beaten KC three straight at Mile High. Risk: Walker ran for 173 on this run defense in Week 1.

NE@MIA.reason: Maye has finished QB1, QB1, QB3 and QB2 the past four weeks and faces a Miami defense with six sacks all season, which blunts the two missing guards. Miami ranks 27th in points per drive and 29th in score rate with Willis at QB; A.J. Brown's Saturday status is the swing.

PHI@WAS.reason: The Eagles are 1-6 ATS, start McKee with Hurts on IR, lost Smith and Wicks, and play a short week against a Washington team off its bye. This 5.5 beats the books' 6, and Smith and Wicks are both out. Payne and Kinlaw out invite Barkley, the lone risk.

CHI@SEA.reason: Chicago has scored 30 or more in every game Williams started and finished, has the rest edge off Thursday and adds Simmons inside. Seattle's offense is not rolling and Byron Murphy is questionable; three is the key number, and Seattle's defense is the reason this is not a top-five play.

MIN@DET.reason: Minnesota's undefeated 6-0 defense is elite at generating pressure and disguising coverages, while Detroit is missing top safety Kerby Joseph. With Aaron Jones and Brian O'Neill cleared to play, the Vikings have enough balance to stay inside the key number of three even with Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown active for the Lions.

LV@NYJ.reason: The Jets are banged up in the trenches with T'Vondre Sweat, Joseph Ossai, and Max Mitchell ruled out, and Breece Hall questionable with a quad injury. Despite a four-game skid against a tough schedule, the Raiders are the healthier, better-coached squad and shouldn't be catching points here.

ARI@DAL.reason: Saving the crucial half-point off the current -7 market line makes Dallas the clear side against a vulnerable Arizona run defense allowing over 126 yards per game. Even without KaVontae Turpin and Dee Winters, Dallas's offense will score too efficiently for an Arizona unit missing OL Jon Gaines II and DL Walter Nolen.

ATL@TB.reason: Atlanta's upset of the 49ers last week was fueled by a +4 turnover margin despite being outgained by 1.5 yards per play. Even with rookie WR Emeka Egbuka out, Baker Mayfield and the Bucs' superior defense should handle an inconsistent Falcons squad beneath the key field-goal number.

BAL@BUF.reason: Getting the hook on a historical field-goal rivalry where the last three meetings were decided by three points or fewer is prime SuperContest value. Lamar Jackson carries no injury designation returning from his ankle issue, and Buffalo has key questionables across the board in Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore, and Spencer Brown.

IND@JAX.reason: Indianapolis is shipping off talent in a rebuild, but laying nearly double digits with an inconsistent Jacksonville squad is overpriced. Power-rating models put this closer to JAX -6.5, so there is solid line value holding our noses with the divisional underdog.

TEN@CIN.reason: Tennessee just waved the white flag on their season by trading cornerstone DT Jeffery Simmons to Chicago, and they will also be without offensive playmakers Tyjae Spears and Carnell Tate. Cincinnati ranks top-eight in both scoring offense and scoring defense, setting up a decisive blowout at Paycor Stadium.

CLE@PIT.reason: Returning from Paris with no bye week puts a 22-PPG Steelers offense in a sluggish spot for a gritty AFC North divisional grinder with a 39.5 total. First-place Cleveland has covered five straight divisional games, making the hook above a field goal very valuable.

LAC@LAR.reason: The winless Chargers cannot get out of their own way and will now be without star safety Derwin James, Deane Leonard, and guard Kayode Awosika. Backing Sean McVay's surging Rams aligns with the biggest power-rating edge of the week.

KC@DEN.reason: Following an embarrassing 20-3 loss to Seattle, the Chiefs get Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, and OT Jaylon Moore cleared to play. Meanwhile, Denver is missing safety Talanoa Hufanga and RB RJ Harvey, with OT Garett Bolles and DL Zach Allen questionable.

NE@MIA.reason: New England is missing both starting guards and likely plays without A.J. Brown (missed Thursday/Friday practice), while RB TreVeyon Henderson is battling an illness. Miami got its first win last week, and Malik Willis's rushing ability should keep the Dolphins inside a full touchdown at home.

PHI@WAS.reason: While Washington's defensive interior is depleted without Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw to slow Saquon Barkley, the Eagles have dropped five straight and are decimated with DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, and Jonathan Jones all out. Coming off a bye with a half-point discount vs. the current -6 market, Washington pulls away late.

CHI@SEA.reason: Thursday's blockbuster acquisition of Jeffery Simmons immediately upgrades a 5-2 ATS Bears defense facing a Seattle interior where DT Byron Murphy is questionable and RB Zach Charbonnet is limited. Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze are clicking well enough to take this heavyweight NFC clash down to the wire.

MIN@DET.reason: Vikings' historically elite defense (league-best points allowed ~12.3 PPG, #1 in multiple advanced metrics) should keep the undefeated club competitive on the road against a high-scoring Lions team; power-rating models see only a 1-point Lions edge.

LV@NYJ.reason: Home Jets get the slight edge in a matchup of struggling teams, and the Raiders have been inconsistent.

ARI@DAL.reason: Cowboys' higher-powered offense at home should exploit a weak Cardinals defense (2-5, poor point differential); the market and power-rating models both land near this number.

ATL@TB.reason: Close game between middling NFC South sides; Tampa's home field and a slight model lean offset Egbuka being out.

BAL@BUF.reason: Bills and Josh Allen at home off the bye face a Ravens team with Lamar returning (full practice, no designation) but still not fully sharp.

IND@JAX.reason: Large number against a struggling Colts squad; power-rating models have Jacksonville only ~6.5 points better.

TEN@CIN.reason: Titans are depleted (Spears and Carnell Tate out) against a solid Bengals team with Burrow playing well; power-rating models land exactly on the number.

CLE@PIT.reason: Home division game for the Steelers after the Paris trip; power-rating models see them nearly 6 points better and their defense is solid even if the offense averages ~22 PPG.

LAC@LAR.reason: Winless Chargers (0-6) missing Derwin James face a better Rams team at home; the biggest power-rating gap from the market (model ~10.4).

KC@DEN.reason: Tight AFC West matchup; power-rating models have Denver a slight favorite, and the Broncos have been solid at home despite Harvey and Hufanga out (Rice/Kelce cleared for KC).

NE@MIA.reason: Clear talent gap against a depleted Dolphins side (Achane out for the season), despite A.J. Brown being questionable and some OL issues.

PHI@WAS.reason: Eagles without Jalen Hurts (out for the season, Tanner McKee starting) and missing top WRs (Smith and Wicks out); Barkley plays but the Commanders get the home edge and model support.

CHI@SEA.reason: Seahawks home edge against a strong Bears team; power-rating models are basically on the number, a close call with limited edge.

MIN@DET.reason: Power-rating models make Detroit closer to a one-point favorite than 3.5; Kerby Joseph is out and Roger McCreary is questionable, although Gibbs and St. Brown are available. I like Minnesota's ability to keep this within a field goal.

LV@NYJ.reason: The short home number is reasonable. Breece Hall is questionable and David Bailey doubtful, so I wouldn't make this a high-confidence play.

ARI@DAL.reason: Arizona has significant concerns in the trenches, with guard Jon Gaines out, defensive tackle Walter Nolen out and center Hjalte Froholdt questionable. Dallas has its own absences, but I prefer laying the Westgate 6.5 rather than the seven appearing elsewhere.

ATL@TB.reason: Tampa gets the home-field advantage, and Baker Mayfield and Chris Godwin are available; Emeka Egbuka is out, but Atlanta also loses Brian Robinson and has several defensive players questionable. Power-rating models support the favorite.

BAL@BUF.reason: Lamar Jackson has no game designation and practiced fully, which makes Baltimore dangerous with more than a field goal. Buffalo has several questionable contributors, including Spencer Brown and Dalton Kincaid, but Baltimore's offensive-line concerns keep this from being a stronger pick.

IND@JAX.reason: This is where the Colts' late-week trades matter: losing Nelson and Buckner weakens both sides of their line. Nine and a half is a big number, but I believe Jacksonville has a better chance of creating a decisive trench advantage than the earlier power ratings suggest.

TEN@CIN.reason: Tennessee has traded away Jeffery Simmons and is also without Tyjae Spears and Carnell Tate; Calvin Ridley remains questionable. Cincinnati has Ja'Marr Chase available, and I expect the Bengals to exploit Tennessee's reduced depth.

CLE@PIT.reason: I respect Pittsburgh's home-field advantage, but Cleveland is 5-2 and has the defense to keep this close. Coming back from the Paris game last week and averaging roughly 22 points per game offensively, Pittsburgh doesn't convince me to lay more than a field goal.

LAC@LAR.reason: This is my strongest favorite: power-rating models project the Rams near -10, and the Chargers are 0-6 while missing Derwin James, guard Kayode Awosika and defensive back Deane Leonard. I see a substantial matchup advantage for the Rams.

KC@DEN.reason: I think Denver is undervalued at home. Pat Surtain II is expected to return, although Hufanga and RJ Harvey are out and four Broncos remain questionable; Kansas City's Rice, Kelce and Moore are available.

NE@MIA.reason: Seven points is a lot to lay with New England given A.J. Brown's questionable status after missing the final two practices and the absence of both starting guards from the active roster. Miami's offensive-line injury is a concern, but I prefer the points.

PHI@WAS.reason: Philadelphia is missing DeVonta Smith, Wicks, Campbell and Jonathan Jones, significantly reducing its available receiving and defensive options. Washington's losses of Payne and Kinlaw are important, especially with Barkley available, but I still like the Commanders at -5.5.

CHI@SEA.reason: Seattle's acquisition of Quenton Nelson improves its offensive line, but Charles Cross and Anthony Bradford did not practice Friday, while Charbonnet was limited. Chicago's acquisition of Simmons strengthens the case for taking the points, although his immediate integration is an uncertainty.
